feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong CV with clear senior-level positioning, credible progression, and relevant digital strategy depth. It reads polished and substantive, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with limited quantified outcomes beyond scope metrics; a few style/grammar inconsistencies also reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, culminating in director and consulting roles, which strengthens credibility and leadership narrative.  
- Strong domain alignment: digital strategy, Drupal/CMS modernization, analytics, multimedia, and advocacy communications are consistently reinforced.  
- Good use of scale indicators such as “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers,” which adds impact.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements: include results tied to traffic growth, engagement, conversion, efficiency, cost savings, or team performance, not just responsibilities and platform scope.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to improve structure and save space.  
- Fix writing/style inconsistencies: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; punctuation in lists is inconsistent (e.g., “web, email, social, and multimedia” vs. other non-Oxford-comma lists); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “A2 (learning)” instead.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it’s slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and adding a sharper value proposition will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with your seniority and strongest differentiators: digital strategy, platform modernization, and operational systems for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Reduce the long channel list; “multi-channel” or “cross-channel” already covers web, email, social, and multimedia.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving multi-channel communications, web modernization, and content operations for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, editorial workflow design, and platform governance, with a strong track record translating policy and technical issues into clear, accessible content. Experienced in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and building scalable systems that improve execution across teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows/systems” are repeated in Core Competencies.
- “Advocacy messaging” and stakeholder coordination also appear elsewhere; keep the intro higher-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level language: “Multi-channel communications leadership” instead of “Multi-channel communication”; “Web platform governance” instead of “Web & CMS administration.”
- Reduce overlap and group related ideas more strategically, e.g.: Digital strategy & transformation • Editorial systems & governance • Web platform modernization • Analytics & performance reporting • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- Consider swapping “Workflow & systems architecture” for “Content operations & workflow design” if you want clearer alignment with recent roles.
- Keep style consistent: use plural nouns where appropriate (“communications”), and avoid mixing admin-level and leadership-level phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with Header (“cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” “workflows and systems”).
- Also duplicates Topline Skills and Soft Skills, especially stakeholder coordination and multimedia production.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a service list rather than a high-impact consulting entry. Tighten the bullets, foreground strategic outcomes, and avoid repeating NACo achievements already covered in prior roles and Recent Projects.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper positioning line: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, content operations, Drupal platform improvements, and AI-enabled member discovery.”
- Convert task-heavy bullets into 3–4 outcome-oriented bullets; start with strong verbs like “Designed,” “Built,” “Led,” “Advised.”
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/properties supported, workflow improvements, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search accuracy/engagement gains, or time saved.
- Combine overlapping technical points, e.g.: “Built Drupal campaign experiences, modular microsites, and member toolkits while providing front-end implementation and troubleshooting for public-facing web properties.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- The AI search, microsite, and anniversary/campaign work already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level unless you add distinct outcomes.
- Governance, analytics, and enterprise web improvement overlap with the Director of Digital Media role; emphasize consultant-level advisory scope and new initiatives.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize enterprise ownership and outcomes while avoiding overlap with the earlier NACo role’s newsletter/video execution details.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the strongest achievements into sharper, results-led bullets: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight more outcome-focused: add growth, engagement, efficiency, or audience metrics for email/social if available; otherwise shorten that bullet.
- Tighten operations language: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio and expanded analytics/reporting across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, strengthening decision-making, governance, and publishing standards.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current email/newsletter and recurring video language overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, platform modernization, and systems.
- “Governance/publishing workflows” also appears in the consultant role; vary phrasing or attach a concrete outcome here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads broad and overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize what you owned at this level.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy campaigns and organization-wide editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet outcome-oriented: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing with ownership: “Built cross-team editorial planning processes across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving publishing coordination and workflow consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Improved digital publishing workflows” overlaps with the Director role’s governance/publishing standards; keep this at the process-execution level, not enterprise governance.
- Weekly video/livestream language also appears in the 2015–2018 role; frame this here as scaling an existing format rather than originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it largely repeats the header and Core Competencies. Make it sharper, more senior, and more distinct by emphasizing leadership scope and governance rather than generic communications phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Replace with tighter, less repetitive language:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience and journey-based content planning
- Consider upgrading “messaging” to “communications” to sound more strategic and less tactical.
- If space allows, align wording to proven strengths from recent roles: “enterprise web modernization” or “governance for 10,000+ page environments.”
- Keep each line noun-based and parallel; avoid mixing leadership terms with execution terms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” overlap heavily with the header and Core Competencies.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” is close to “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies; use one phrasing only.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it currently reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent execution themes rather than repeat every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as capability-led, not tool-led: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older-signal items here, especially “jQuery,” unless it is central to current target roles.
- Put the strongest, most recent differentiators first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/workflow automation.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “Drupal platform delivery for large public-facing sites” or “CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector web properties.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Drupal,” “WordPress,” “SharePoint,” and “Power Pages” are already listed in Technical + IT; avoid repeating the full stack here.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” and “workflow automation” also echo Core Competencies, so keep wording tighter or more specific.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT.” In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic analytics capability and decision-making impact, not just platforms.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Analytics strategy and reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive/leadership dashboards • SEO, UX and performance analysis”
- Put the most differentiating items first: analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting; tools second.
- Tighten wording: change “Leadership reporting” to “Executive dashboards/reporting” and “SEO and performance analysis” to “SEO, UX and performance analysis.”
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work elsewhere in the CV, such as “analytics infrastructure for 10,000+ page site” or “reporting for organization-wide decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool stack.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and several NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and make it feel more senior than task-based.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: **Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems**
- Drop “video editing” unless editing is a target-role requirement; it reads more execution-level than leadership-level.
- Consider “multi-camera production systems” instead of just “PTZ camera systems” to broaden the skill and avoid sounding too narrow/tool-specific.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this skill area to scale in experience bullets instead of here (e.g., studio buildout, recurring advocacy programming, event support).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- This item duplicates evidence already shown in Director of Digital Media and Digital Media Manager / Producer, so keep it concise and distinct.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, scannable list, but it’s generic and slightly redundant with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Since Drupal is central to recent roles, this item should emphasize platform depth/order rather than just naming tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider **Drupal (enterprise, migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** if brief qualifiers are allowed.
- If space permits, add one impact cue tied to recent work: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsite builds)** to reinforce seniority and scale.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; use either plain platform names everywhere or add qualifiers consistently across technical sections.
- If this section is meant to be purely technical, consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it reflects meaningful production use.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider consolidating or differentiating this section as “Platforms used” vs. “Capabilities.”
- Drupal already appears repeatedly in recent experience, so avoid over-explaining it here.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Make it more current and implementation-focused by emphasizing tools you actively use in recent roles and grouping them more strategically.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • Integrations & tagging: APIs, Google Tag Manager • Edge/serverless delivery: Cloudflare Workers • Deployment & automation: GitHub Actions”
- Drop version numbers unless they matter; “HTML” and “CSS” are usually cleaner than “HTML5/CSS3.”
- Order by relevance to recent work: APIs, GTM, Cloudflare Workers, and GitHub Actions likely signal more senior, current capability than jQuery.
- If accurate, add one proof point elsewhere in experience, e.g., “implemented API-driven features,” “deployed edge scripts via Cloudflare Workers,” or “automated web workflows with GitHub Actions.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing.
- “API integrations” and “workflow automation” also overlap with Topline Skills, so vary wording or keep this section tighter.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function and keep only strongest, most relevant tools: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier • Project/issue management: Jira, Asana • Collaboration: Slack, Teams”
- Drop lower-signal or older/general tools unless central to recent work: Basecamp, Trello.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier to show application: “used to build cross-team publishing, intake and reporting workflows.”
- Consider renaming the heading to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” for clearer alignment with recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating them elsewhere without added context.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; listing both can dilute stronger technical signals unless collaboration platforms are a hiring priority.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. It should either signal level of use/ownership or be tightened so it doesn’t repeat the email leadership already covered in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for specificity and consistency: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic Thrive Marketing • Mailchimp**
- If space allows, add a light qualifier to show practical depth: **Email campaign platforms, marketing automation and member engagement systems: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic Thrive Marketing • Mailchimp**
- Keep the newest/most enterprise-relevant platform first; Dynamics 365 should lead as the strongest current signal.
- Only include platforms you used directly in recent roles; remove any tool with limited or outdated exposure.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters and multi-channel communications; avoid adding descriptive claims here unless they introduce new technical depth.
- “Engagement Systems” may partially overlap with “Automation & Workflow Systems”; keep this item focused on email/marketing platforms only.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads like a setup role rather than showing concrete contributions. Tighten it around team-building, platform work, and content production with clearer outcomes if you can add metrics.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground advancement and scope: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Split execution from impact: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, to expand the organization’s in-house publishing capacity.”
- Make supervision more direct: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or “supervised one digital media associate,” if accurate.
- Add metrics where possible: number of livestreams/videos, audience growth, email/social output, site traffic impact, or production turnaround improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching or early-building the format.
- Avoid repeating broad “workflows across web, email, social” language already used in later, stronger roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with one clear differentiator—the first podcast launch—but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize initiative, cross-functional coordination, and any concrete outputs.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer outcome-oriented line, e.g., “Produced digital and multimedia content that translated research and policy work into member-facing communications.”
- If possible, add scale or results: number of episodes, audiences reached, stakeholders supported, or types of projects delivered.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles so progression is clear; 1–2 lines is enough.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content/multimedia production” language already covered more strongly in the 2015–2024 NACo roles.
- “Overseeing planning, scripting, and production” overlaps with later video/studio leadership; keep the focus here on the podcast launch and research/program support.
